  • META setup into Monday — Enrich watching for a clean move over $648 on a rounded base, buyers ACTIVE
  • LLY pushing $1,450 — Enrich: former resistance became support; biotech acceleration + AI drug discovery as a decade theme
  • Bitcoin's week closes Sunday — Remz: a finish under the 200-day at 73K puts the 58–60K lows next; back over 73K and “it's a different chart”

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
Friday's tape closed a week the group is still processing — and the weekend posts split into two camps. Prof supplies the bear-market frame: “Mag 4 in a bear market. $GOOGL sitting down 26%. $NVDA sitting down 32%. $META sitting down 20%. $TSLA sitting down 22%. Meanwhile $SPY is down 3.5%” (his numbers; our computed drawdowns are GOOGL 26.54%, NVDA 31.93%, META 17.48%, TSLA 20.34%, SPY 3.17%) — and his Saturday-night post sets the mood: “I think we can all agree that 2026 has been one of the most exhausting trading years in a long time. Nonstop headlines. Failed breakouts. Bull traps. Violent selloffs. And just when you think the market is finally finding its footing, something else comes along.” (quoted to the visible cutoff). Remz asks the weekend's open question — “Are markets preparing for a bigger selloff? $BTC. Could Bitcoin be signaling something bigger for the broader markets?” — and his annotated chart makes the case: six red weeks in a row since 87K, straight through the 200-day at 73K, with the 58–60K lows next if the week closes down. Peter answers it the other way: “Downside volume gap filled bitcoin:native. Should see a strong bounce in the coming weeks.” Enrich is the third voice on Bitcoin and the negative one: “Bitcoin didn’t become what society envisioned. Closer association to ‘scam’ than ‘security’.” The constructive camp is Enrich on stocks: “$META strong setup into Monday, watching for a clean move over $648. Nice rounded base on the daily chart. Buyers have been ACTIVE + relative strength off the charts” — and “$LLY it was, in fact, time. Former resistance became support. Now pushing $1,450”, with the biotech-acceleration thesis behind it (“AI’s impact on drug discovery is a major reason why. Eli Lilly will be at the forefront”). His other weekend post is the discipline note: “Some weekend hopium for the AI buildout bagholders. I’ll take it. Price can fall while the business gets stronger. The key is owning companies where that’s actually happening. Buy quality. Keep checking the thesis.” Venu adds the education piece that frames the whole tape: “Why a Stock Can Rally 20% and Still Be in a Stage 4 Downtrend. One of the biggest mistakes investors & traders make during market corrections is confusing a sharp rally with the beginning of a new uptrend. A stock can decline 40%, rally 20%, and still remain in Stage 4.” (quoted to the visible cutoff) — and then his second round of earnings reversals: FISV (“Stage 1 base with a Power Earnings Gap, potential Stage 2”), DUOL (“Flat base + wedge breakout”), APP (“Earnings gap, reclaimed 200-day SMA”) and TOST (“Beautiful cup formation”), each with a new chart. Sean and iain post no tickers this window — Sean tells his story (“I once lost $200k in a single day… By 2023 I had a few hundred dollars left & had dropped out of college”) and iain starts another (“About 16 months ago, I met a trader who was making way more money than me”). Your process gives three genuine qualifiers with triggers above the close: META (rounded base, Enrich's $648), LLY (breakout holding above former resistance, Enrich's $1,450) and DUOL (wedge breakout, Venu's 167.01) — plus FISV (range top 65.15), APP (repair in progress, 412.82) and TOST (cup forming, 36.97) as pending, not confirmed. The declines, not entries: NVDA at a new 52-week low into Tuesday's earnings, GOOGL 26.54% under its high, and BTC under the 200-day with the group split on the bounce. The extended names: AAPL printed a new 52-week high at 356.27 with no pullback, and LLY sits 12.65% above its 50-day EMA — the LLY setup is the $1,450 level holding, not a pullback entry. The discipline is in the framing: the indexes gave back ground and QQQ is the weakest of the four, but the strongest-looking names are breaking out — and Tuesday's NVDA print is the next test.

  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels. META's trigger 648.00 is Enrich's stated level; LLY's trigger 1,450.00 is Enrich's stated level and its invalidation 1,301.63 is his chart level; FISV's trigger 65.15, DUOL's 167.01 and APP's 412.82 are Venu's chart levels; TOST's trigger 36.97 is the 3-month swing high; BTC's trigger 73,000 and invalidation 58,000 are Remz's stated levels (the 200-day and the 58–60K lows).
